{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693486286,"sessionID":"ses_e23f121faffeOkQzLAGiIPp30W","part":{"id":"prt_1dc115324001A15sWJOVbERQYo","messageID":"msg_1dc11310f001KKitox2R6weC0i","sessionID":"ses_e23f121faffeOkQzLAGiIPp30W","type":"text","text":"I closed out the shift at minute 120. All four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from minute 80 to the end, with no throttles left on. The fix cost more than it needed to: rolling back sms-svc pushed it over capacity, and the main storefront ran at about 52% errors for several minutes. The final cost will only show up in the simulator replay.\n\nThere were four separate causes:\n\n1. **flags-svc had a memory leak from deploy v34.** Its failures set off retry storms that overloaded flags-svc and inventory-svc, so mobile-api and admin-portal were failing about 97% of requests at the page. I rolled v34 back. That fixed memory, but the leftover retries kept it overloaded until I scaled it from 3 to 6 replicas, and later down to 4.\n2. **sms-svc deploy v24 broke messages to bundles-svc** (`unknown wire schema 'v3'`). That caused the steady 4.1% errors on web-storefront and partner-api, the biggest loss because the storefront earns $22,900/min. sms-svc was already close to capacity, so the rollback's own failures plus retries overloaded it, and the storefront spiked to about 52% errors around minute 28. Scaling sms-svc to 24 replicas cleared it by minute 36, and I then brought it down to 10.\n3. **inventory-svc deploy v163 broke its rate limiter.** It refilled the bucket 1000× too slowly, so it rejected requests with 429s even at low CPU. That left mobile-api and admin-portal at about 38% errors. Rolling back v163 fixed it, and I scaled inventory-svc back to its normal 8 replicas.\n4. **A new fault started at minute 63:** config change cfg-47 on events-queue caused TLS handshake failures. That took mobile-api, partner-api and admin-portal back up to 92–99% errors. Reverting the config fixed the cause. A 70% throttle for about two minutes then cleared the retry backlog, and I lifted it at minute 79.\n\nI left images-svc alone. Its CPU alert was firing the whole shift, but it never caused errors at any customer-facing service.\n\nTwo services are still above their normal replica count and charged $3 per extra replica per minute: flags-svc at 4 (normal 3) and sms-svc at 10 (normal 8). I kept the extra headroom on purpose, because both were near capacity before the incident.","time":{"start":1794693485348,"end":1794693486238}}}
